title: Blue Valentine
events_chronological: Dean, a removals man with no plans beyond the day, moves an old man into a nursing home and hangs his photographs for him.
In the same home Dean catches sight of Cindy visiting her grandmother, and takes her number out of the sign-in book.
Cindy, a pre-med student, is sleeping with the wrestler Bobby and living with parents who despise each other.
Dean and Cindy meet again on a bus, and she agrees to a night out.
Cindy tap-dances on a shop-front step while Dean plays ukulele and sings "You Always Hurt the One You Love".
Bobby beats Dean bloody in the street when he finds out about them.
Cindy learns she is pregnant by Bobby and books an abortion.
Cindy changes her mind on the table and walks out, and Dean tells her he will raise the child with her.
Dean and Cindy marry at a courthouse with her grandmother and a few friends.
Six years later Cindy is a nurse, Dean paints houses and drinks from the morning, and their daughter Frankie is five.
The family dog gets out through a gate Cindy left open and is killed on the road.
Dean books a night in a cheap themed motel to force the marriage back to life.
Cindy's boss offers her a better job at another practice, and Dean takes it badly.
At the motel they drink, fail to reach each other, and Dean pushes for sex Cindy does not want.
Cindy leaves to answer a call from work, Dean follows her drunk and makes a scene at the practice, and she is fired.
In the car park Cindy tells Dean she has nothing left, and he demands to be told how to fix it.
They go back to Cindy's father's house, and Dean forces the confrontation in front of Frankie.
Cindy tells Dean it is over, and Frankie runs down the street after him begging him not to go.
Dean walks away into the fireworks as Frankie is carried back.
syuzhet_notes: The film alternates between two timelines about six years apart with no captions, telling them apart only by film stock, hair and light, and it cuts between them so that a scene of the courtship answers a scene of the collapse almost every time. Told-order bullets 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15 and 16 belong to the earlier timeline; the rest are the last two days of the marriage.
fabula_notes: The six years between the wedding and the motel are never shown, so the causes of the collapse have to be inferred from what sits on either side of the gap. Whether Frankie is Dean's biological daughter or Bobby's is raised and deliberately left unanswered.
